Catsimatidis Warns Foreign Adversaries Could Target Trump

On Friday, speaking with FOX Business’ Cheryl Casone on "Mornings with FOX Business," Catsimatidis argued that foreign rivals have an incentive to undermine Trump because of his tough negotiating approach.
“The evil empire, whether it’s Russia, North Korea, China, Iran, the evil empire will do anything to make sure that they cripple Trump in the Nov. 3 election,” Catsimatidis said.
Catsimatidis, chairman and CEO of
Red Apple Group

, said Trump’s background as a businessman shapes his approach to international negotiations, potentially making him a greater obstacle for countries seeking economic or geopolitical advantages over the U.S.
"He’s not only a president, he is a businessman," Catsimatidis said.

Catsimatidis also singled out Canadian Prime Minister
Mark Carney
, saying he was disappointed with the Canadian leader despite describing him as smart and someone he likes.
"I think he [Carney] feels the same way, that they’re gonna be able to take a bigger advantage of the United States if Trump was crippled," Catsimatidis said.

Catsimatidis Warns of Another 9/11
Reflecting on the 25th anniversary
, Catsimatidis said he lost four friends and a cousin in the attacks.
He warned that younger Americans who did not experience 9/11 firsthand should not become complacent about national security threats.
"I believe that our country is under attack and that if we don’t keep our eyes open, there’ll be another 9/11," he said, adding that New York and Washington remain potential targets.
Catsimatidis ended with a direct appeal to voters: "Nov. 3, help save America, because we’re under attack in so many directions."
Catsimatidis is best known as the owner of the New York City supermarket chain
Gristedes
. He has an estimated net worth of $6.2 billion, according to Forbes.
Catsimatidis’ Oil, Real Estate Empire and Trump Donations
He also owns
United Refining
, a Pennsylvania-based oil refinery he acquired out of bankruptcy, along with real estate holdings in New York and other markets.

In 2024, the Republican real estate and oil tycoon made his largest political contribution yet, donating $2.4 million to support Trump and congressional Republicans — nearly double what he gave in 2016, according to The Washington Post.
Trump Approval Hits New Low as GOP Support Slips
Trump’s approval

params.linkText: rating has fallen to a new low

children: amid the Iran war in the latest NBC News poll, with signs of weakening support among Republicans.
Trump’s approval stands at 36%, down one point from the spring survey, while his disapproval rating has risen to 64%, the highest in the poll.
More concerning for Trump, support among Republican voters has also slipped. His approval among Republicans fell to 80% from 83%, while the share who strongly approve dropped to 41% from 52%.

It marks the first time in NBC News polling that fewer than half of Republicans strongly approved of Trump. The spring poll was conducted in March and April, while the latest survey ran from Aug. 20 through Sept. 1.
